official.deadline_central_display: November 15, 2026 (KMSP application in WiSH); November 1, 2026 (UW-Madison Early Action admission)
official.deadline_note: Candidates must apply to UW-Madison under Early Action by November 1, 2026 and submit the separate King-Morgridge scholarship application in the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH) by November 15, 2026 for Cohort 11 (Fall 2027 entry).
official.status_note: The KMSP site publishes the November 1, 2026 International Admissions deadline and the November 15, 2026 WiSH KMSP application deadline for Cohort 11; the Fall 2027 KMSP application opens in WiSH by late August.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholars receive a full-time, four-year/eight-semester scholarship to the University of Wisconsin-Madison that includes tuition and fees, on-campus room and board, health insurance, airfare, and a stipend for miscellaneous expenses.
eligibility: Incoming first-year, undergraduate, bachelor's degree-seeking student with no prior tertiary education at another institution
Apply to UW-Madison Early Action and receive an admit decision in the Early Action review period
Demonstrate a high level of financial need
Demonstrate a commitment to poverty alleviation and community development, and plan to return to the home country/region after graduation
Hold a high school diploma or equivalent from an institution in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia
Diploma received on or after November 1, 2023, or in the final year of study with expected completion prior to August 1, 2027
requirements: Maintain a minimum 3.0 grade point average
Complete at least 12 credits as a full-time student each semester

Actively participate in program activities including individual advising appointments, program meetings, and other scheduled programming; respond to KMSP communications in a timely manner and submit absence requests to the program manager in advance
Participate in Orientation and the Wisconsin Experience Seminar during the first fall semester
Be a good citizen of the general University community, following all university policies and state and federal laws
documents: UW-Madison undergraduate admission application (Early Action) with all required materials
UW-Madison NetID created from the Campus ID sent in the application confirmation
King-Morgridge Scholars Program application in the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH): eligibility short-answer questions plus a 500-700 word essay
selection_criteria: Holistic review of school and community involvement, essays, the connection between degree interests and professional aims, commitment to poverty alleviation and community development, and first-generation status
Scholarship decisions released by the end of March
application_method: Apply to UW-Madison under Early Action by November 1, then submit the separate King-Morgridge scholarship application in the Wisconsin Scholarship Hub (WiSH) by November 15; both applications are required for full consideration
official.application_route: Two required applications: UW-Madison Early Action admission (Nov 1) and the KMSP application in WiSH (Nov 15).
official.citizenship_residency: Must hold a high school diploma or equivalent credential from an institution in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, or Southeast Asia (official eligible-country lists apply)
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is for international students from the eligible regions listed by UW-Madison
official.description: The King-Morgridge Scholars Program is a four-year, full-tuition scholarship for enterprising, creative, dedicated students committed to applying their talents toward poverty alleviation around the globe; scholars join from countries in Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, and Southeast Asia, and the programme is made possible through generous gifts by the King and Morgridge families.
official.program_type: Donor-endowed university scholarship for international undergraduates

verification.notes: KMSP and UW-Madison admissions pages confirm coverage components, Cohort 11 deadlines (Nov 1 admission / Nov 15 WiSH), six awards per year, eligible regions, and published expectations; no monetary value is published for the award.

applicant_utility.summary: KMSP is effectively a full ride for six students a year from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, South Asia, and Southeast Asia, and it hinges on two applications: UW-Madison Early Action by November 1, 2026 and the KMSP application in WiSH by November 15, 2026 - only students admitted in the Early Action review period are eligible. Write the 500-700 word essay around how your intended degree connects to poverty-alleviation work you will carry back home, and remember that a high level of financial need is a stated criterion, so document it honestly.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year international applicants from eligible regions with strong academics, real financial need, and a credible plan to fight poverty in their home country after graduation.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply to UW-Madison Early Action by November 1 and complete all required application materials
Set up your NetID from the Campus ID sent in your application confirmation email
Complete the WiSH multiple-choice questions to unlock the KMSP opportunity, then submit the short answers and 500-700 word essay by November 15
Gather transcripts from an eligible-region institution well in advance - UW-Madison grants no deadline extensions
Prepare evidence of financial need and community involvement for the holistic review
common_rejection_risks: Missing the Early Action window - only Early Action admits are eligible for the scholarship
Prior tertiary education or an already-completed post-secondary degree, which makes applicants ineligible
An essay that states passion for development without linking degree plans to home-country impact
Assuming the WiSH application extends the admission deadline - both dates are hard and no extensions are given
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Personal and discretionary spending beyond tuition, fees, room and board, health insurance, airfare, and the miscellaneous-expenses stipend is not covered.
document_audit: Two separate submissions are required - admission via UW-Madison and scholarship via WiSH; one does not trigger the other
Transcripts must come from an institution in the eligible regions and meet first-year entry requirements
The KMSP essay is capped at 500-700 words - overshooting signals you cannot follow instructions
alerts: Only six scholarships are awarded per year and decisions arrive by the end of March
Failing the 3.0 GPA, the 12-credit full-time load, or participation expectations can terminate the scholarship
Transfer students, graduate applicants, currently enrolled UW-Madison students, and students who have completed a post-secondary degree are not eligible
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: UW-Madison Early Action application (Nov 1) -> WiSH KMSP application with 500-700 word essay (Nov 15) -> holistic review by Admissions and KMSP staff -> decisions released by the end of March.
